errors.quote: and ramping to peak within replica cold-start times in the fast half of its bursts.
errors.stated: In the faster half of the vision-pool bursts (i.e. at least 50% of episodes), baseline-to-peak ramp completes within replica cold-start time.
errors.computed: tex/trace-eda.tex:289-294 publishes the onset distribution over the 18 episodes: median baseline-to-peak = 6 min, 10th percentile = 2 min, fastest = 1 min; and states only that 'the fastest onsets (1--2 minutes) are comparable to or faster than replica cold-starts of tens of seconds to minutes'. 'Fast half' = onsets <= the median = <= 6 min = 360 s. The thesis's own realizable encoder lead range is 15--165 s (intro.tex:264, closedloop.tex:446/468-469), so a 360 s onset is 360/165 = 2.18x LONGER than the longest tested cold-start lead. The claim only holds for the fastest decile (2 min = 120 s < 165 s), i.e. ~10% of bursts, not ~50%.

errors.quote:
reporting 25--41.3\%
serving-cost savings (fewer GPUs at SLO, from 3.3--5.5$\times$ higher
throughput) via modality-aware placement and
scaling~\cite{Qiu2025ModServe}
errors.stated: 25--41.3% serving-cost savings are attributed, parenthetically, to 3.3--5.5x higher throughput.
errors.computed: The parenthetical invites the reader to reconcile the two ranges and it fails by roughly a factor of two. If a throughput gain of G reduced the GPU count at fixed SLO, the cost ratio would be 1/G: 1/3.3 = 0.303 -> 69.7% savings; 1/5.5 = 0.182 -> 81.8% savings. The stated savings 25--41.3% correspond to cost ratios 0.750 and 0.587, i.e. implied throughput gains of only 1.33x and 1.70x -- 2.5x to 3.2x smaller than the quoted 3.3--5.5x. Also note the direction pairing is inverted as printed: the LARGER saving (41.3%) should pair with the LARGER throughput gain (5.5x), but 41.3% -> 1.70x while 25% -> 1.33x, so neither endpoint maps onto either quoted throughput endpoint.
errors.relation: internal recomputation: cost saving = 1 - 1/throughput_gain, within one parenthetical
errors.propagates_to: None; the ModServe cost/throughput figures appear only here in related.tex.
errors.proposed_fix: Decouple the two figures rather than presenting one as the cause of the other: 'reporting 25--41.3\% serving-cost savings via modality-aware placement and scaling, and separately up to 3.3--5.5$\times$ higher image-encoding throughput~\cite{Qiu2025ModServe}'. (Confirm against the ModServe paper which stage the throughput gain is measured on; the parenthetical as written asserts an equivalence its own numbers do not support.)

'four ingredients ... plus the evaluation modality' (line 355) matches tab:rel-positioning: Modality disagg. / Per-pool signals / Forecast scaling / Calibrated simulation = 4, plus Real-cluster GPU eval. = 5 body columns. 'three precedence claims' (line 326) matches the three enumerated claims ('The first claim is therefore', 'Second, zero-shot', 'Third, a silicon-calibrated'). CROSS-CHAPTER NUMERIC AGREEMENT -- R^2 = 0.123 (lines 188, 335) reproduces tex/trace-eda.tex:241 verbatim; R^2 = 0.654 for decode (line 335) reproduces trace-eda.tex:245 verbatim, and its rounding to 0.65 in conclusion.tex:18 is correct. Hurst 'up to ~0.93' (line 207) is verified as the MAXIMUM of all six rows of tab:eda-persistence (0.83, 0.86, 0.87, 0.76, 0.91, 0.93) and is verified to belong to the images/s (vision) row, so both halves of that claim hold. 'Fano factor growing by nearly three orders of magnitude with window size' recomputes as 938/1.8 = 521.1, log10 = 2.72 -- 'nearly three' is a fair description (and 938 itself is 10^2.97 above the Poisson value of 1, so the claim holds under either reading). notes: This chapter contains only six thesis-owned numeric quantities; every one is a forward reference, so the audit is a pure consistency exercise against trace-eda.tex, predictors.tex, closedloop.tex and apendice.tex. All six reproduce their source values exactly -- there is NO arithmetic error in the chapter. The six findings are, in descending importance: (1) a genuine overclaim about burst-onset speed vs cold-start lead ('fast half' where the data supports only the fastest decile), which propagates to intro.tex:167 and is load-bearing for the necessity half of the thesis argument; (2) a scope error attributing the request-arrival Fano growth to the per-signal demand set and calling it 'strongest in the vision signal', which the EDA chapter never computes per signal; (3-6) denominator, version-pin, external-citation and precision-drift issues that are ambiguities rather than wrong numbers. The external figures (ModServe 25--41.3% / 3.3--5.5x / 79% predictor error, SageServe ~25% GPU-hours, WarmServe 5 minutes, BurstGPT 213 days) cannot be settled from the thesis text; only the ModServe cost/throughput pair admits an internal recomputation, and that recomputation fails, which is why it is reported. The most reviewer-exposed unresolved item remains the 79% ModServe predictor error at line 104: it motivates the entire forecasting contribution and this thesis's own best 1-minute image WAPE is 52.9% (tab:pred-wape), so the two must be shown to be the same metric on the same signal or the implicit comparison is unsound -- that check requires the ModServe paper and was out of scope for this text-only pass.
